title: Colors broken in fzf preview on Windows (mintty)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have read through the manual page (`man fzf`)
- [x] I have searched through the existing issues
- [x] For bug reports, I have checked if the bug is reproducible in the latest version of fzf

### Output of `fzf --version`

0.56.3 (tarball)

### OS

- [ ] Linux
- [ ] macOS
- [x] Windows
- [ ] Etc.

### Shell

- [x] bash
- [ ] zsh
- [ ] fish

### Problem / Steps to reproduce

Syntax and line highlighting produced by bat are incorrectly displayed by fzf preview on mintty:
`#> echo | fzf --preview="bat --theme=1337 --highlight-line=2 --color=always test.sh | tee out.txt"`
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9eb1cecb-5a7a-4e2c-bb4c-09cbb5906762)
`#> cat out.txt`
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/740d71ad-dada-4c91-947b-88c29de9e2c4)

The issue is also reproducible on Alacritty and ConEmu.
Colors are kept intact only on Windows Terminal, but it is unusably slow and laggy.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Does `bat --theme=1337 --highlight-line=2 --color=always test.sh` itself produce the right colors?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I don't know if the behavior is related to my problem, but it seems that fzf is not passing the current appearance to bat or it's not available anymore. Even if I run fzf with --color=dark. fzf --preview="bat --theme-dark='Catppuccin Mocha' --color=always {}" If I specify the theme directly, everything works as expected: fzf --preview="bat --theme='Catppuccin Mocha' --color=always {}"; Many thanks for your work!!!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Does `bat --theme=1337 --highlight-line=2 --color=always test.sh` itself produce the right colors?

Yes, output is similar to shown by `cat out.txt`.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> I don't know if the behavior is related to my problem

Yes, this is the same problem: fzf somehow transforms color codes received from bat.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
It is probably because of `winpty`. Can you try setting `export MSYS=enable_pcon`?

https://github.com/participant1/fzf/blob/243a76002c93b474cf8401b37670a43803a0a2d2/src/winpty_windows.go#L18-L44

Related:
* https://github.com/participant1/fzf/pull/3806
* https://github.com/participant1/fzf/issues/3809

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Can you try setting `export MSYS=enable_pcon`?

Same result. It's not only mintty related, but also reproducible with Alacritty and ConEmu.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> > I don't know if the behavior is related to my problem
> 
> Yes, this is the same problem: fzf somehow transforms color codes received from bat.

I don't think it's the same problem. He said "If I specify the theme directly, everything works as expected".

@participant2 It looks like 'bat' somehow fails to detect the terminal theme (dark or light) when run inside the preview window of fzf. `--dark` option of fzf only changes the colors of fzf, and it does not do anything beyond that.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> everything works as expected

It seems that together with bat's theme-dark problem, it just happened that 'Catppuccin Mocha' theme colors are not that much warped by fzf pass-through. But there are still slight differences in colors, and `--highlight-line`, if specified for bat, is not highlighted in preview window with this theme.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant1 You're completely right!
It depends on the BAT_THEME.

```shell
# .zshenv
# Bat setting
export BAT_THEME=""
export BAT_THEME_LIGHT="Catppuccin Latte"
export BAT_THEME_DARK="Catppuccin Mocha"
export BAT_STYLE="full,-grid,-header-filesize,-header-filename"

# Starship Palette
export STARSHIP_PALETTE_LIGHT="catppuccin_latte"
export STARSHIP_PALETTE_DARK="catppuccin_mocha"

# Starship Palette & BAT_THEME
x=$(defaults read .GlobalPreferences AppleInterfaceStyle 2>/dev/null)
if [[ $x = "Dark" ]]
  then
    STARSHIP_PALETTE=$STARSHIP_PALETTE_DARK
    BAT_THEME=$BAT_THEME_DARK
  else
    STARSHIP_PALETTE=$STARSHIP_PALETTE_LIGHT
    BAT_THEME=$BAT_THEME_LIGHT
fi

Hopefully i can remove this after a new release of bat.
https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/pull/3168

> NOTE: You have to _export_ (typeset -gx) the BAT_THEME, so fzf can find it.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Thanks for confirming it's not related problem, @participant2.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> and `--highlight-line`, if specified for bat, is not highlighted in preview window with this theme.

Can you elaborate? `--highlight-line` doesn't affect the preview window. It just change the highlighting of the current selection in the list section.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: `--highlight-line` is an option to `bat`, expected effect can be seen on the second screenshot in the description. When passed through `fzf`, it disappears (first screenshot).

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I see, I was confused because it's also an option of fzf. Anyway, `fzf --preview="bat --theme=1337 --highlight-line=2 --color=always {}"` works fine on my Macbook. Also tested with the tcell library used for Windows binaries. I don't have a Windows PC to test it, but at least fzf doesn't seem to be doing something wrong.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I've made quick debugging through fzf to tcell, and, for Windows case, tcell seems to have nothing in between of 16 colors and 24-bit colors. So, for my `TERM=xterm-256colors` case,  setting `export TCELL_TRUECOLOR=enable` just worked and resolved the issue. I think this issue can be closed, and, readdressed to tcell in future, if using `TCELL_TRUECOLOR` workaround on Windows is not enough for some reason.
Thank you for taking a look at this!
